record.original_question: Let F={α_1,...,α_k} be a finite set of affine functions α_i(x)=m_i x+a_i with integer parameters m_i≥2 and a_i≥0. For a nonnegative integer z, let E[F:z] be the smallest subset of {0}∪N containing z and closed under every function in F. For each of the following triples, prove or disprove that E=E[{α_1,α_2,α_3}:0] has asymptotic density 0: (1) α_1(x)=2x, α_2(x)=3x+3, α_3(x)=6x+10; (2) α_1(x)=2x, α_2(x)=6x+3, α_3(x)=3x+2; (3) α_1(x)=3x, α_2(x)=2x+2, α_3(x)=6x+15; (4) α_1(x)=3x, α_2(x)=6x+2, α_3(x)=2x+1; (5) α_1(x)=6x, α_2(x)=3x+1, α_3(x)=2x+2; (6) α_1(x)=6x, α_2(x)=2x+1, α_3(x)=3x+6.

evidence.quote: Let A={α 1,...,α k}be a set of aﬃne functions α i(x) = m i x+a i with m i, a i integers and m i≥2, a i≥0,for i= 1,...,k. Let z be a nonnegative integer. Let E[A:z] denote the smallest subset of {0} ∪ N containing z and closed under the functions given in A.

Problem. Here are some challenging questions stated in [K1]. T o prove or to disprov e that the density of E=E[{α 1, α 2, α 3}: 0] is 0 in each one of the following cases : 1. α 1(x) = 2 x , α 2(x) = 3 x+ 3 , α 3(x) = 6 x+ 10. 2. α 1(x) = 2 x , α 2(x) = 6 x+ 3 , α 3(x) = 3 x+ 2. 3. α 1(x) = 3 x , α 2(x) = 2 x+ 2 , α 3(x) = 6 x+ 15. 4. α 1(x) = 3 x , α 2(x) = 6 x+ 2 , α 3(x) = 2 x+ 1. 5. α 1(x) = 6 x , α 2(x) = 3 x+ 1 , α 3(x) = 2 x+ 2. 6. α 1(x) = 6 x , α 2(x) = 2 x+ 1 , α 3(x) = 3 x+ 6.

artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on Klarner's affine-closure density problems (notably Lagarias's "Erdős, Klarner, and the 3x+1 Problem") describe these specific three-generator cases with multipliers in {2,3,6} as still unresolved. No proof or disproof of density zero has been published for any of the six listed cases.

status_evidence.title: Erdős, Klarner and the 3x+1 Problem (Lagarias slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Klarner raised the problem: Do any of these semigroups have orbits of positive density? This is an unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Klarner density question for these affine-generated orbits remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Erdős, Klarner, and the 3x+1 Problem - American Mathematical Monthly
status_evidence.snippet: Describes problems on semigroups of integer affine maps and the integer sets they generate, with history, partial solutions, and new unsolved problems.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists these affine-closure density questions among open problems.
